title: Usage dispute flow and provisional credit lifecycle for enterprise invoices
creator: Riley Chen
description: Problem statement: Enterprise customers occasionally raise invoice disputes that require provisional credits while the billing team investigates. Current ad-hoc workflows create inconsistencies: temporary credits are applied without standardized expiration, reserved capacity vs usage overage counts are handled differently, and retroactive token adjustments (e.g., due to model versioning or reruns) lack a clear lifecycle. This ticket defines a repeatable product flow and automation for: 1) intake and validation of usage disputes, 2) issuance and expiration of provisional credits, 3) interaction rules with reserved capacity/commit bands, 4) audit trail and notifications, and 5) guardrails to prevent negative balances or double refunds.
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake workflow that support agents can follow (confluence link in artifacts) and a front-line support UI hook to flag invoices as 'under dispute'
Automated provisional credit issued within 24 hours for qualifying disputes, with configurable TTL (default 45 days) and automatic reconciliation after investigation completes
Provisional credits do not reduce reserved capacity usage counters; they adjust billed amounts only and are visible on invoice line items with an audit token

Clear rules for retroactive token reconciliation when a model/version re-count changes historical usage: system either issues adjustment credit OR generates a corrected invoice depending on magnitude (>5% or >$1k triggers corrected invoice flow)
No customer-facing negative balance beyond their legal credit limit; system caps provisional credit at customer's unused reserved-commit balance + $10k unless manual approval
A complete audit trail entry for every provisional credit and final resolution with links to investigation artifacts and approver identity
Support for overlapping workflows: if a refund has been issued and later a provisional credit is applied, refunds are netted against credits and documented in order of action
API and console surfaces for enterprise customers to view disputes, provisional credit status, and expected resolution date
comments: 2025-01-16 — Riley Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: stakeholders from Billing, Legal, Customer Support, Eng (metering), and PM present. Agreed provisional credit TTL should be configurable per-customer. Action: PM to draft acceptance criteria.

2025-01-21 — Asha Patel: Spoke with two enterprise CS reps. Common root causes: unexpected model switch (customer defaulting to higher-rate model), duplicate batched job, and data-exfil protection throttling leading to retry storms. Need ability to tag dispute reason code.

2025-01-29 — Priya Nair (Eng - metering): Technical constraint: we can generate corrected token counts only up to 90 days back without heavy compute. For >90d cases, we should rely on sampling + manual review and legal signoff.

2025-02-03 — Legal (M. Torres): Recommend provisional credits be non-interest-bearing and documented with CLI of approval; require checkbox for 'customer acceptance of corrected invoice' when generating corrected invoice.
2025-02-10 — Asha: Prototype UI mock uploaded to Drive (link in artifacts). Support queue will expose a 'Dispute intake' button that triggers provisional credit flow and notifies finance queue.

2025-02-17 — Eng (Billing infra): Proposal to implement provisional_credit objects in billing ledger with TTL and state transitions: pending -> applied -> reconciled -> archived. We need to add unique audit_token for each action.

2025-02-19 — PM: Updated acceptance criteria to include netting logic for refunds and provisional credits to avoid double-pay. Added cap enforcement for provisional credit issuance. Noted security review required due to audit and KMS involvement.
notes: Edge case: customer with pooled org credits and multiple sub-org invoices — credit should attach to invoice-level but previewed against org-level commitments to avoid double-apply
Edge case: automated provisional credits issued during pending chargeback windows (payment processor dispute) must be flagged and coordinated with finance; include a payment_processor_dispute code
Trade-off: shorter TTL reduces outstanding liabilities but increases support load; default 45 days chosen after stakeholder poll (Finance leaned toward 30, CS toward 60)
Implementation detail suggestion from Eng: represent provisional credits as negative invoice line items with a separate 'provisional_credit_id' and column 'reconciled_at'
Rollout plan: feature gated behind enterprise toggle; pilot with 5 customers (high-usage and varied billing models) for 6 weeks before org-wide release
